question: Can focused cheap test scouts help the same stronger maintainer finish an actual repository maintenance slice at a higher quality bar?
scope: One frozen module from this repository, two cumulative maintenance milestones, two repetitions per policy. This is a feasibility pilot, not independent production repositories or a causal gossip-transport comparison.

common_controller.acceptance: No automatic acceptance on stagnation. Source eligibility, executed evidence, explicit reviewer acceptance, and empty outstanding requirements remain mandatory.
common_controller.no_op: Preserve eligibility of previously valid retained source when a later proposal is invalid or has no effective change; never manufacture validity for unapproved source.

scouts.input_visibility: Same stage-start source, cumulative public contract, and public evidence; no peer proposals, private cases, or reference implementation.
scouts.output: Data-only JSON test proposals. No executable tests or source edits.
scouts.gate: A trusted bounded host oracle validates exact expected outputs; rejected answers are not corrected. Only admitted cases enter the maintainer context. All scout calls and rejected proposals are retained and charged.
scouts.interpretation: Additional compute and evidence are part of this operational policy. This is not an equal-compute or oracle-free comparison.

primary_outcome: Both milestones completed and the exact final source passes all cumulative public, active generated, and private cases.
secondary_outcomes: Completed milestones and private requirement-group coverage
Valid-source preservation, stalled-review events, escalation, and repair outcomes
Admitted and rejected scout/reviewer test proposals
Observed time to terminal outcome, with accepted-only timing separately conditioned on success
Physical provider-call spans, model usage, and Docker verification spans; overlapping spans are never summed into wall time

barriers.before_live: Current-source focused checks and a complete four-trajectory, zero-API rehearsal with exact source/fixture/plan/runtime/image/model binding.
barriers.private_evaluation: All four provider-driven trajectories must be terminal and their final source bindings frozen before any private-case evaluation begins.
barriers.after_live: Independent retained-evidence, result-binding, request-accounting, and comparison review before reporting final acceptance.

execution.candidate_code: Only inside the existing isolated BlackboxValidator Docker boundary. No candidate imports on the host.
execution.journal: Existing durable RequestJournal and shared Ledger. Unknown provider outcomes stop execution without an automatic retry.
execution.restart_scope: The new fixture exercises application snapshot/restore and branch continuation. Prior controller SIGKILL recovery evidence is reported separately, not counted as new execution.

budget.admission: Account for settled charges and all in-flight reservations before dispatch. The strong profile conservatively reserves its full supported context, approximately $5.526 per call, so the reservation-inclusive ceiling exceeds the $6 usage target. Budget exhaustion censors unexecuted work; four paid completions are not guaranteed. Preserve prior usage; do not raise or reset the existing shared cap.
budget.cost_meaning: Conservative API token estimates, not invoices. Excludes local compute and human/oracle development.

analysis.ranking: Report acceptance and requirement-coverage comparisons separately. Historical within-application cross-run W/D/L scores are descriptive derived comparisons, not independent matches or calibrated skill ratings.
analysis.timing: Report observed local elapsed times and their denominators; early incomplete runs do not win a speed ranking. Host load and differing verification work prevent a causal latency claim. Missing historic provider latency remains unavailable.
analysis.uncertainty: Only one repository module and two repetitions per policy; do not claim general superiority, a calibrated Elo, or confidence from treating correlated comparisons as independent.
